sections.h2: Who do I deal with on a Gallatin County tax bill?
sections.html:
Three Warsaw offices come into play when a house changes hands. The PVA places the value, the Sheriff's Office takes the money, and the County Clerk files deeds and takes assessment appeals.

  • PVA: 200 Washington Street (mail to PO Box 470), Warsaw, KY 41095, phone (859) 567-5621.
  • Sheriff: 106 North Main (mail to PO Box 1025), Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5751. The county's sheriff page links to a tax bill lookup.
  • County Clerk: 803 East Main Street, Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5411, open weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon.

The City of Warsaw runs its own online payment page for water, sewer and property tax bills, so a house inside the city limits may owe the city as well as the county. Ask both the sheriff and the city which bills attach to an address before you set a closing date, and keep copies of every paid receipt for the buyer's title company. A clean paper trail shortens the closing, because the title search will list any unpaid balance as an exception.

sections.h2: What makes Gallatin County unusual for a home sale?
sections.html:
Size, mostly. Gallatin County covers 105 square miles in all, which makes it the second smallest county in Kentucky. It sits on the Ohio River across from Indiana and counts as part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area. The legislature formed it on December 14, 1798 out of Franklin and Shelby counties, and the later creation of Owen, Trimble and Carroll counties left it about a tenth of its first size.

The county has three communities: Warsaw (the seat), Sparta and Glencoe. Every resident was counted as rural in 2020. Interstate 71 passes through with three exits around Sparta and Glencoe, joined by US 42 and US 127, and Wikipedia reports that by the 1980s more than half of local workers held jobs elsewhere. The commute still averages 29.5 minutes.

River engineering and racing give the county its landmarks. Markland Locks and Dam was built from 1956 to 1964 and a hydroelectric plant was added in 1967. The county's own website pitches the Kentucky Speedway and two river marinas. A county-owned airport one mile north of Sparta, with a 5,000-foot runway, opened in June 2023.

Here is who lives in the county. Population was 1,291 in 1800, 7,870 in 2000, 8,589 in 2010 and 8,690 in 2020, when the median age was 39.5 and 25.2 percent of residents were under 18. Census estimates put the share of residents 65 or over at 17.5 percent, against 20.6 percent in Floyd County, so a smaller slice of Gallatin County owners can claim the age-based homestead reduction. Census estimates put 84.6 percent of adults as high school graduates, 15.0 percent as holding a bachelor's degree, and 87.4 percent of households as having broadband.

sections.h2: How does Gallatin County's housing market measure up?
sections.html:
Prices sit between the mountain counties and the capital region, and the county has grown slowly but steadily.

About 61.3 percent of adults are in the labor force. Employer-business jobs fell 7.4 percent between 2022 and 2023, to 1,373, and retail sales reached roughly $135 million in 2022. The 2020 census found 3,685 housing units with 13.1 percent unoccupied, so a share of the stock is seasonal, vacant or waiting for a buyer.

sections.h2: When does the sheriff want Gallatin County property tax?
sections.html:
Bills are payable to the sheriff, and the state's collection rules in KRS 134.015 give every owner the same ladder. A 2 percent reduction applies to a bill paid in full by November 1, the printed amount runs through December 31, and late payers owe 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward.

If bill mailing slips, the Department of Revenue can replace the usual dates with a compressed schedule of one month at a discount, one month at face and one month at 5 percent, so read the dates printed on the bill itself. When a house sells, tell the sheriff the new owner's name so later bills reach the right person.

sections.h2: How do Gallatin County owners dispute a value?
sections.html:
Start at 200 Washington Street. The state requires a PVA conference before any appeal, and visits are easiest right after assessment notices arrive. The tax roll then opens to public view for 13 days in early May.

Once you have met the PVA or a deputy, the County Clerk's office takes your written appeal, which is due by the end of the next business day after viewing closes. The local board of assessment appeals sits about four to five weeks later, for up to five days.

  • Bring facts about the land and buildings, construction costs, insurance details and sale listings of similar properties.
  • Expect to explain your evidence in person with the PVA also present.
  • The board must put the reason for any raise or cut in writing, and you are allowed to record the hearing.

An owner who files but does not attend the hearing cannot continue to the Kentucky Claims Commission, so mark the hearing date on a calendar the day it is set.

sections.h2: How much does the homestead exemption save in Gallatin County?
sections.html:
For seniors and totally disabled owners, $49,100 is deducted from assessed value in 2025 and 2026. File with the Gallatin County PVA. Applied to the county's typical home value of $178,200, the taxable figure drops to $129,100.

Disability filers need payments from a federal or retirement-system program covering the whole assessment period, and they renew every year. Service-connected veterans and people ruled totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems are exempt from that yearly renewal.

sections.h2: What if taxes are unpaid when a Gallatin County house sells?
sections.html:
The balance stays with the property. KRS 134.015 calls the tax a personal debt as of the assessment date, and a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 continues no matter who takes title.

On April 15 the sheriff transfers open bills to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency. Within 30 days the county attorney mails a first notice, a second follows within 60 days, and the Department of Revenue says the clerk's tax sale takes place 90 to 135 days after the transfer. A third-party buyer at that sale can pile on substantial fees. Ask the sheriff at (859) 567-5751 for a payoff before you list, and plan to clear it from the sale proceeds.

faqs.q: Where do I send a Gallatin County property tax payment?
faqs.a: Send it to the Gallatin County Sheriff, 106 North Main in Warsaw, or PO Box 1025, Warsaw, KY 41095. The county's sheriff page links a tax bill lookup.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Gallatin County PVA?
faqs.a: Call (859) 567-5621 or visit 200 Washington Street in Warsaw. The PVA handles value questions, exemption forms and owner records.

faqs.q: Is Gallatin County's early-payment date different from other counties?
faqs.a: No. It follows the statewide date of November 1, when full payment earns 2 percent off. The face amount is owed through December 31.

faqs.q: Does the City of Warsaw send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: Warsaw offers an online page for water, sewer and property tax bills. Owners inside the city should ask the city and the sheriff which bills apply to their address.

faqs.q: Does a tax lien survive a sale in Gallatin County?
faqs.a: Yes. A delinquency lien stays on the property after a sale until the tax is paid or the period in KRS 134.420 runs out, so settle the balance at closing.
